scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (a jerk) for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just needs to work 35 hours a week whenever it's convenient for her. She can work from the office or home sometimes. She has a full benefits package, which is great, especially since she's under what most people consider full-time. She also has a nice retirement package, and the company pays for continued education. She works in cutting-edge robotics and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year, and her boss even lets employees "earn up" more PTO if they work extra hours one week. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the officeâĢĶlike a $500 espresso maker, fancy coffee, nice furniture, etc. They're also paid well, with a pretty middle-of-the-road salary for robotics, but she says the work-life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner, and honestly, a mid-range robotics salary is still damn good. At first, I thought, "Good for her" for finding something she's happy with. But recently, it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. For example, when we're out with my friends or just hanging out, she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, all the vacations she takes, how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie and then came back and worked a little later. It seems like she forgets that this isn't a normal job. Last night, we were at a party, and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon. One of the people at the party asked, "Don't you have work?" and she said, "Yeah, but I can set my own hours." That rubbed me the wrong way, and I told her she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks because it was obnoxious and came off as braggy. She said she was just explaining something, and I said it wasn't just this one thingâĢĶit was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives. She said I was coming off as jealous and that it was a bad look. She said she's where she is because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. Instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it and stormed off. So, am I being AITA for what I said? First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA stands for "am I the asshole?" It's a way to ask if you're being unreasonable or unfair in a situation. So, am I being the asshole here? Let me break it down. My girlfriend has a great job with a lot of perks. She's happy with it, and she's proud of what she's achieved. That's understandable. However, I feel like she's bragging about her job perks, especially in social settings, and it's making me uncomfortable because most people don't have the kind of job she does. When she mentioned setting her own hours and touring apartments during the workweek, it seemed like she was flaunting her flexibility, which not everyone has. That made me feel like she was comparing her life to others in a way that made me jealous or envious. She, on the other hand, feels like I'm being jealous and that I should focus on my own goals instead of complaining about her. She's proud of her achievements and doesn't see the issue with talking about them. So, is it wrong for me to want her to be less braggy? Or is it reasonable for me to feel uncomfortable when she talks about her job perks in a way that makes me feel like she's forgetting how most people live? I think it's important to consider both perspectives. On one hand, she's proud of her job and her achievements, and she has the right to talk about them. On the other hand, I have the right to feel uncomfortable when she talks about her job in a way that makes me feel like she's forgetting the reality of most people's lives. Maybe the issue isn't that she's talking about her job perks, but how she's talking about them. If she's doing it in a way that's making me feel inferior or envious, then it's understandable that I'd want her to be more mindful of how she discusses her job. However, she might feel like I'm being overly sensitive or that I'm projecting my own insecurities onto her. She might think that she's just sharing her positive experiences and that I should be supportive instead of critical. So, is wanting her to be less braggy about her job perks a reasonable request, or am I being AITA for feeling that way? I think it's a bit of both. It's reasonable to want her to be more considerate of how her words make me feel, especially if it's causing friction in our relationship. However, it's also important for her to feel proud of her achievements and to share them without feeling like she's being criticized. Maybe the solution is to have a conversation where we both express our feelings without blaming each other. I can explain that her talking about her job perks makes me feel like she's forgetting how most people live, and she can explain that she's proud of her job and doesn't mean to make me feel bad. In the end, it's about finding a balance where both of our feelings are respected. I don't want to come off as jealous or controlling, and she doesn't want to feel like she can't talk about her job. It's a delicate situation, but with open communication, we can work through it. So, am I being AITA? I don't think so. I'm expressing my feelings and wanting her to be more mindful of how she talks about her job. It's not about being jealous or controlling; it's about wanting our relationship to be harmonious and understanding. However, I can see how she might feel that way if I'm not expressing my feelings clearly or if I'm coming off as critical instead of concerned. It's important to approach the conversation with empathy and understanding to avoid making her feel attacked. In conclusion, while I'm not entirely AITA, there's room for improvement in how I communicate my feelings to her. By approaching the conversation with empathy and a willingness to understand her perspective, I can address the issue without being the asshole.
